claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent reaches 90.9% Task-Space F1 and 99.4% human audit pass rate
claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent achieves a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, outperforming direct task induction (79.2–80.0%) and prior-guided induction (85.1%); 994 of 1,000 sampled items from correctly identified tasks pass human audit.

evidence_spans.source_text: As shown in Table 1, BIR-mediated construction achieves 90.9% Task-Space F1, compared with 79.2–80.0% for direct induction. Providing T0 improves direct DeepSeek-V4-Flash induction to 85.1% F1, while MedBenchAgent further increases precision from 76.9% to 87.0% at the same 95.2% recall, reducing false positives from six to three.

To assess whether these constraints are preserved in the finalized benchmark, we sample 1,000 items without replacement and audit each for reference groundedness, task–query alignment, unambiguity, and evaluation integrity against its annotation evidence and specification. An item passes only when all four criteria are satisfied. Table 2 shows that 994 items pass, yielding a 99.4% consistency rate.

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: Demonstrates domain portability and uncovers fine-grained VLM performance variations
claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further demonstrate portability to a specialized medical domain and evaluate twelve VLMs, revealing task- and setting-specific variation obscured by aggregate scores.

evidence_spans.source_text: To assess the cross-domain portability of MedBenchAgent, we apply the complete construction workflow under a specialized medical setting using ISIC 2018 (Codella et al., 2019; Tschandl et al., 2018), with a distinct dataset and annotation schema.
We evaluate twelve VLMs spanning general-purpose and medical-domain model families, multiple parameter scales, and different inference regimes.

To quantify such changes, we compare all 66 model pairs and find that 12–24 pairs (18.2–36.4%) reverse ordering between Overall Acc. and individual-task Acc.; within tasks, 4–15 pairs (6.1–22.7%) reverse between Acc. and F1.

Spatial rankings also change across imaging settings. BreastGPT-8B leads Qwen3-VL-32B on BUS-BRA detection, with Acc@IoU0.5 of 82.80 versus 62.08, whereas Qwen3-VL-32B leads on VinDr-Mammo detection, with 12.86 versus 0.90 (Table 4).

claims.label: supported
claims.claim_summary: All tested methods achieve 100% evidence-mapping agreement on matched tasks
claims.claim_text_verbatim: All methods achieve 100% EMA on matched tasks.

evidence_spans.source_text: Their matched tasks have supporting-field mappings consistent with the reference, as reflected by the EMA results in Table 1.

For each matched task, agreement was assigned a value of one when the method-proposed supporting-field set was identical to the supporting-field set confirmed during review against the dataset annotation schema Σm, and zero otherwise. FPs and FNs were excluded from the EMA denominator.
